reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
commonErrors: Counting pupil size or anisocoria instead of reactivity.
Calculating GCS-P from a GCS with a non-testable component.
name: GCS-Pupils Score

version.label: GCS-P (Brennan, Murray & Teasdale 2018)
version.detail: GCS total minus the Pupil Reactivity Score (number of unreactive pupils). Range 1–15. Uses the Glasgow structured approach for the GCS.

purpose: A single index combining GCS and pupil reactivity to describe early severity after traumatic brain injury.

calculatorNotice.title: Components first
calculatorNotice.message: GCS-P requires all three GCS components and an assessable pupil response. If any is non-testable, no GCS-P is reported.

inputDefinitions.label: Eye opening (E)
inputDefinitions.help: Check for factors that interfere, observe, then stimulate: sound before physical pressure.

options.label: None
options.detail: No opening at any time, no interfering factor.

options.label: Orientated
options.detail: Correctly gives name, place and date.

options.label: None
options.detail: No audible response, no interfering factor.

inputDefinitions.label: Best motor response (M)
inputDefinitions.help: Record the best response; test the arms.

options.label: Localising
options.detail: Brings hand above clavicle to stimulus on head or neck.

options.label: Normal flexion
options.detail: Bends arm at elbow rapidly; features not predominantly abnormal.

options.label: Abnormal flexion
options.detail: Bends arm at elbow; features clearly predominantly abnormal.

options.label: None
options.detail: No movement in arms or legs, no interfering factor.

inputDefinitions.label: Pupil reactivity to light
inputDefinitions.help: Only reactivity counts; pupil size does not enter the calculation.

notTestable.label: GCS-P not reported
notTestable.summary: A GCS component or the pupil response is not testable, so GCS-P is not reported.

resultStates.label: Severe range
resultStates.detail: Correlate with airway, respiratory, neurological and systemic assessment, according to the clinical situation and local protocol.

resultStates.label: Above the severe range
resultStates.summary: Lower values indicate more severe injury.
resultStates.detail: Interpret with the components, pupil findings and imaging.

resultStates.label: No impairment measured
resultStates.summary: No impairment measured by GCS-P at this assessment.
resultStates.detail: Describes consciousness and pupil reactivity only; it does not exclude intracranial injury.

clinicalContext.text: Extends the GCS with pupil reactivity, which carries prognostic information the GCS does not.

clinicalInsights.text: Pupil unreactivity lowers GCS-P below the GCS total.
Report the GCS components, the pupil findings and the GCS-P together.

limitations.text: Derived in traumatic brain injury; not validated as a general coma measure.

limitations: Adds pupil reactivity only, not size or asymmetry.
The authors' probability charts (combining GCS-P with age and CT) are not reproduced.

confounders.factor: Ocular trauma or prior eye surgery
confounders.effect: Can make pupil reactivity unassessable or misleading.

guideSections.what: GCS total minus the number of unreactive pupils, giving a 1–15 index.
guideSections.howToPerform: Assess E, V and M with the structured approach and each pupil's reaction to light. PRS = number of unreactive pupils. GCS-P = GCS − PRS.
guideSections.clinicalContext: A severity index for communication and research; individual prognosis needs the full clinical picture.

sources.citation: Brennan PM, Murray GD, Teasdale GM. Simplifying the use of prognostic information in traumatic brain injury. Part 1: The GCS-Pupils score: an extended index of clinical severity. J Neurosurg. 2018;128(6):1612-1620.
Teasdale G, Jennett B. Assessment of coma and impaired consciousness. A practical scale. Lancet. 1974;2(7872):81-84.

licensing.note: Official GCS aids and the authors' probability charts are not reproduced.
